meaning.zh:
“竖起耳朵” 或 “留心听” 。

这个短语来源于狗或马当它们听到一些新奇或者感兴趣的声音时，会竖起耳朵的行为。因此，当人们使用这个短语时，其意思是要注意听，集中注意力。例如，在老师即将宣布考试重点时，会用这个短语提醒学生认真听讲。
meaning.en: This phrase originates from the behavior of dogs or horses who perk up their ears when they hear something interesting or unusual. Therefore, when used on people, it means to pay attention or listen carefully. For example, a teacher might use this phrase to remind students to listen closely when announcing exam topics.

lines.en: When the teacher said there would be a surprise quiz, everyone *picked up their ears*.
lines.zh: 当老师说会有一个突击测验时，每个人都竖起了耳朵。

lines.en: If you *pick up your ears*, you might catch some useful information.
lines.zh: 如果你竖起耳朵，你可能会听到一些有用的信息。

lines.en: She always *picks up her ears* when she hears gossip.
lines.zh: 每当她听到八卦时，她总是竖起耳朵。
